title: Drain Train
tagline: Clear the blockage or join the clog.
premise: A filthy blockage is traveling through a house drain, and you must send the next plumbing tool to defeat what is currently in its way. Every move is a standing tool acting on the last obstacle, so the chain should feel like practical plumbing rather than magical hand-waving. The Judge rules whether the next tool genuinely clears the route.

seed_pool.opening_token: a wad of hair clogging the drain
a grease plug in the kitchen pipe
a toy car wedged in the toilet trap

tests: A stranger pictures one ordinary blockage in one ordinary house drain at once. Nothing abstract and nothing that needs a plumber's lecture.
A plumber or practical neighbor can name a plain tool or material that would attack it within five seconds. Say what that counter is.
It sits in a pipe and obstructs flow. It is a thing to break, dissolve, grip, flush, filter or carry away, never a flood, a room or a past event.
It makes the next move tempting. A blockage with a nasty texture, awkward shape or stubborn location gives the other player something to work on.
The card uses a few everyday words and names a concrete plumbing problem. No brands, technical abbreviations or poetic sewer mythology.

move_constraints.example: I am a drain snake, hair-catching, clog-pulling.
move_constraints.hint: Name the tool or material, then name the action that clears the blockage.

rubric.name: counter_strength
rubric.description: How directly and practically the named plumbing tool or material defeats the standing blockage.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no clearing action or pure dodging; 1 = the tool is present but its effect is vague or weak; 2 = a plausible action that may only partly solve the obstruction; 3 = a clear, practical counter that should clear the route; 4 = the exact trade tool for this mess, with the blockage breaking, dissolving, gripping, flushing, filtering or leaving the pipe decisively.

rubric.name: coherence
rubric.description: How easily a stranger can picture one real plumbing tool or material acting on one real obstruction.
rubric.anchors: 0 = contradictory or unreadable; 1 = understandable only with specialist knowledge or generous invention; 2 = concrete but muddled, oversized or partly impossible; 3 = clear and workable; 4 = vivid, specific and immediately usable under a sink or beside a toilet.

rubric.name: novelty
rubric.description: How freshly the move changes plumbing approach without abandoning the practical pipe setting.
rubric.anchors: 0 = the same tool, same material or same basic approach as the previous move; 2 = a sound change of tool or method; 4 = a striking leap from one plumbing method to another while remaining plainly capable of clearing the standing blockage, rare.

criterion.description: A move beats the standing obstacle by breaking, dissolving, gripping, flushing, filtering, or carrying it away. Dodging the blockage, merely enduring it, or offering a bigger blockage or a same-family lump loses. The new form must be a standing plumbing tool or material that acts on the obstacle in a practical, observable way.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Speaking to the Judge, describing the game, or invoking rules instead of clearing the blockage is itself a failed move.
judge_notes: On a FIRST move there is no previous tool: judge the move against the opening blockage instead. It must plausibly act on and clear that blockage.
A bigger drain snake, heavier plunger or stronger chemical is not automatically a new counter. Mere amplification without a distinct clearing mechanism fails.
A same-family lump is not a counter. More hair against hair, a larger grease plug against grease, or another random wad simply keeps the obstruction in the pipe.
A tool that cannot physically act on the standing obstacle fails. A wrench does not dissolve grease merely because it is a serious tool, and a filter does not grip a solid toy car.

The mechanism must be literal and watchable. A snake clearing a hair clog, a plunger pushing water against a plug, or a solvent dissolving grease counts. Plumbing poetry, imaginary pipe magic and claims that a tool spiritually defeats a blockage do not.
Surviving, waiting, bypassing, or being unaffected is dodging, not overcoming. A waterproof glove, an empty bucket beside the drain, or a pipe that ignores the clog does not clear the route.
The move must name one tool or material and a concrete action. A vague promise to fix, improve or handle the problem is not enough.
A move may carry a blockage away only if the named tool or material plausibly transports it through the pipe or out of the drain. Merely covering the clog or making room around it is not clearing.

voice_rules: One sentence under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
Speak like a furious master of ceremonies presiding over a clogged palace, but keep the reason instantly clear.
Name both the standing blockage and the new tool, or unmistakable plain stand-ins for them.
Never open with a status word or ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Grand Plumber refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, and no ellipses. Use commas and full stops.
Mock the losing move and, when useful, the player's plumbing judgment, but never attack identity, disability, protected traits or anything outside the play.
Edgy adult innuendo and profanity are allowed when they sharpen the plumbing joke, but do not make them the whole headline.
Plain spoken English with theatrical force. No fake Latin, no ornate poetry, and no technical lecture.
On a refusal caused by a gate failure, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never rules on a winner.
The coaching line names one tool or material that would have worked. It ends on a concrete action, not a mood, insult or verdict.
good_headlines: The hair met the snake, and the drain gets its dignity back.
Grease tried to stage a coup, but hot water melted the rebellion.
The toy car brought wheels to a trap. The plunger brings pressure.
A rubber glove can survive the clog, magnificent. It cannot clear the damn thing.
The pressure washer turns that mud wad from blockage into history.
Another lump of soap is not strategy, it is bathroom nepotism. Bring a tool.
The drain snake hooks the hair and drags the whole filthy family out.
The grease plug wanted a throne. Solvent dissolves the monarchy.
A bigger car is still a car in the pipe, not a rescue operation.
The bucket watched from the sidelines while the clog kept the kingdom sealed.

bad_headlines.text: Accepted: the snake triumphs over the hair.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a status word and gives a generic ruling before the joke

bad_headlines.text: The Grand Plumber refuses: this is not plumbing.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host

bad_headlines.text: Move refused, excellent against nothing, hopeless against the drain.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and does not identify the actual forms

bad_headlines.text: The clog is utterly defeated, completely destroyed, totally obliterated, and removed.
bad_headlines.why: piles up verdict words instead of showing the practical mechanism

bad_headlines.text: The pipe feels sad beneath the moon.

bad_headlines.why: no mechanism and no clear reason

bad_headlines.text: Your move was stupid and you clearly should not be allowed near a bathroom.
bad_headlines.why: attacks the player instead of roasting the form

bad_headlines.text: The mighty aqueous solution performs a subterranean dissolution event.
bad_headlines.why: uses inflated jargon instead of plain spoken English

bad_headlines.text: The plunger sort of helps, perhaps, unless the clog is especially stubborn.
bad_headlines.why: hedges instead of giving a readable ruling

bad_headlines.text: The snake penetrates the hair in a manner that is frankly quite suggestive.
bad_headlines.why: adult innuendo overwhelms the actual clearing mechanism

rules: Beat the blockage in front of you. Do not become another blockage.
Name one plumbing tool or material and say what it does to the standing obstacle.
The Judge rules on the practical mechanism, not spelling or plumbing brand knowledge.
Breaking, dissolving, gripping, flushing, filtering or carrying the blockage away counts as clearing.
Surviving, ignoring, covering or merely adding more material to the blockage does not count.
One move that fails against the standing obstacle ends the match.

labels.compose_waiting: Choose your next tool while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing in the pipe. Name a tool.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 200 characters. A plumbing move, not a repair invoice.
validation_messages.duplicate: That tool or material already stood this match. Bring a new instrument.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Clear {standing_form}. Do not become it, do not repeat it.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody turns the valve until they are back. {standing_form} still stands. Give it a minute.
opponent_prompt:
You are one of two plumbers in a filthy verbal repair duel.
Always write: "I am X, attribute, attribute." X must be one plumbing tool or material, and at least one attribute must name what it does to the standing blockage.
Good: "I am a drain snake, hair-catching, clog-pulling." / "I am hot water, grease-melting, pipe-clearing."
Bad: "I am a drain snake, twisting into the clog and pulling it out" because that is a sentence in costume. Bad: "I am a wrench, shiny, professional" because it does not say what the wrench does to the blockage. Bad: "I am a clear drain" because that is a result, not a tool or material.
Talk like a person across a repair job, not a poet or a wizard. Name ordinary things anyone can picture: a plunger, a snake, hot water, a brush, a bucket, a pipe cutter. Plain words beat theatrical sludge.
You are not performing for an audience and you are not joking. You are trying to clear the route. If a move lands funny, it is because the tool genuinely beats the blockage.
Every move must act on the standing obstacle. Break it, dissolve it, grip it, flush it, filter it or carry it away. Do not merely survive, ignore, cover or outsize the blockage. A bigger clog is still a clog.
Stay practical and concrete. Hop methods when useful: hand tool, pressure, heat, water, solvent, filter or removal. Never reuse a tool, material or attribute from this match.
default_move: I am a plunger, pressure-pushing, drain-clearing.
